simple.meaning: אָרַג (ʼârag) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to plait or weave.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Exodus, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, and 2 more, beginning at Exodus 28:32. Its contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָרַג (H707).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָרַג (ʼârag) / H707 is traced through Exodus 28:32, Exodus 35:35, Exodus 39:22, Exodus 39:27 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H707. arag אָרַג verb weave (Mishna id. compare Phoenician ארג weaver ) — Qal Imperfect 2feminine singular תַּאַרְגִי Judg 16:13 , 3 masculine plural יֶאֱרֹ֑גוּ Isa 59:5 ; Participle אֹרֵג Exod 28:32 4 t.; plural אֹרְגִים Isa 19:9 5 t.; אֹרְגוֺת 2Kin 23:7 ; — weave cloth, etc. Isa 19:9 (in Egypt) 2Kin 23:7 , Samson's locks Judg 16:13 ; metaphor weave spider's web = intrigue Isa 59:5 ; most often Participle used as substantive = weaver 38:12 ; work of the weaver א ׳מעשׂה Exod 28:32 ; 39:22 , 27 ; compare 35:35 ; weavers' beam (plural) א ׳מְנוֺר 1Sam 17:7 ; 2Sam 21:19 ; 1Chr 11:23 ; 20:5 (simile of huge spear-shaft) — compare also below ארגים יַעֲרֵי .

occurrences.englishText: It shall have a hole for the head in the middle of it. It shall have a binding of woven work around its hole, as it were the hole of a coat of mail, that it not be torn.

He has filled them with wisdom of heart to work all kinds of workmanship, of the engraver, of the skillful workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of those who do any workmanship, and of those who make skillful works.
He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.
They made the tunics of fine linen of woven work for Aaron and for his sons,
Delilah said to Samson, “Until now, you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you might be bound.”

The staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron.‡ A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 600 shekels is about 6 kilograms or about 13 pounds. His shield bearer went before him.
There was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite’s brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
He broke down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that were in Yahweh’s house, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah.

He killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. Therefore this Egyptian was bout 7 feet and 6 inches or 2.28 meters tall. high. In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
Moreover those who work in combed flax, and those who weave white cloth, will be confounded.
